subject: science2
loDesc: Explains Central Dogma of Molecular Biology (Transcription, Translation, Translocation), evidence of evolution (Morphological, Anatomical, Vestigial organs, Paleontological, Connecting links, Embryological), and theories of evolution (Darwinism and Lamarckism).
hookDemo: Display anatomical forelimb bone structures of Human arm, Cat leg, Whale flipper, and Bat wing side by side.
hookAsk: Why do these forelimbs have completely different external functions yet show identical underlying bone arrangements?
streamDo: Observe evolutionary evidences: Appendix, Peripatus, Fossils, Homologous forelimbs, Embryo stages.
streamTask: Classify evidences under Anatomical, Vestigial, Connecting Link, or Paleontological categories.
mountainTask: Explain the step-by-step protein synthesis process: Transcription (DNA to mRNA in nucleus), Translation (tRNA decoding at ribosome), and Translocation (ribosome movement).
skyTitle: Darwin's Natural Selection vs Lamarckism Analysis
skyTask: Critique Lamarck's theory of 'Inheritance of Acquired Characters' using examples and explain why Darwin's 'Survival of the Fittest' gained scientific acceptance.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing Lamarck's 'inheritance of acquired traits' (e.g. stretching neck creates longer necks in offspring) with Darwin's 'natural selection' on pre-existing variations.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'If a weightlifter builds large muscles, do their children automatically inherit big muscles?' Disprove Lamarckian physical acquisition.

crossCurricularLinks: Paleontology & Archaeology: Carbon Dating (Using Carbon-14 radioactive decay to determine age of paleontological fossils)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Traces protein synthesis mechanisms and evaluates structural evidences supporting biological evolution.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use codon wheel charts to simulate mRNA-to-amino-acid translation activities.

subject: science2
fullTitle: Chapter 2: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
loDesc: Analyzes cellular respiration (Glycolysis, Krebs Cycle, Electron Transfer Chain), energy yield from carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids, and compares Mitosis vs Meiosis cell division stages.
hookDemo: Display microscope slides showing onion root tip cells undergoing Mitosis stages (Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase).
hookAsk: In which stage do equatorial chromosome alignment and spindle fiber attachments become clearly visible under a microscope?
streamDo: Observe respiration phases: Glycolysis (Cytoplasm), Krebs Cycle (Mitochondria), ETC Reaction (Mitochondria).
streamTask: Match respiration phases with their specific cellular locations and ATP yield outputs.
mountainTask: Construct a 4-point comparison table contrasting Mitosis (somatic cells, 2n -> 2n) and Meiosis (germ cells, 2n -> 1n, genetic crossing over).
skyTask: Trace glucose breakdown when oxygen is deficient in muscle cells (lactic acid accumulation) versus yeast fermentation (ethanol + CO2 generation).

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Thinking that cellular respiration occurs only in animal cells while plant cells undergo only photosynthesis.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'How do plant cells generate ATP energy at night when there is no light for photosynthesis?'

crossCurricularLinks: Biochemistry & Exercise Physiology: Metabolic Pathways (Tracing aerobic vs anaerobic ATP yield during athletic exertion)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Explains aerobic/anaerobic respiration pathways and compares mitotic and meiotic cell division.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Prepare temporary slides of onion root tips to observe mitosis stages in class.

subject: science2
fullTitle: Chapter 3: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
loDesc: Investigates asexual reproduction (Binary Fission, Multiple Fission, Fragmentation, Regeneration, Budding, Vegetative Propagation, Spore Formation) and sexual reproduction in plants (flower anatomy, pollination, fertilization) and humans (male/female reproductive systems, menstrual cycle, IVF).
hookDemo: Dissect a Hibiscus flower on the demonstration table to expose Sepals, Petals, Stamens (Anther/Filament), and Carpel (Stigma/Style/Ovary).
hookAsk: How does pollen tube growth through the style deliver male gametes into the ovary for double fertilization?
streamDo: Observe organisms: Amoeba, Hydra, Spirogyra, Planaria, Bryophyllum, Mucor.
streamTask: Match organisms with their asexual reproduction mode (Binary Fission, Budding, Fragmentation, Regeneration, Vegetative Propagation, Spore Formation).
mountainTask: Explain four phases of the human 28-day menstrual cycle, detailing hormonal controls (FSH, LH, Estrogen, Progesterone) and uterine wall changes.
skyTask: Explain clinical principles behind Assisted Reproductive Technologies: In Vitro Fertilization (IVF), Surrogacy, and Sperm Banking.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing pollination (transfer of pollen to stigma) with fertilization (fusion of male and female gametes).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Is seed formation complete when pollen lands on stigma, or when male gamete fuses with ovule inside ovary?'

crossCurricularLinks: Endocrinology & Reproductive Medicine: Reproductive Health (Tracing hormonal feedback in menstrual cycles and IVF ART technologies)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Investigates modes of asexual/sexual reproduction in plants and humans, and modern reproductive technologies.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Conduct flower dissection lab practicals for all students.

subject: science2
loDesc: Analyzes ecosystem factors, environmental conservation necessity, biodiversity hotspots, sacred groves, and roles of organizations/laws in environmental protection.
hookDemo: Display a map showing India's Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot alongside pictures of Traditional Sacred Groves (Devrai).
hookAsk: How have indigenous cultural traditions like Sacred Groves protected forest biodiversity for centuries?
streamDo: Observe animal species: Tiger, Lion-tailed Macaque, Lesser Florican, Giant Squirrel (Shekru).
streamTask: Classify species into Endangered, Rare, Vulnerable, or Indeterminate threatened categories.
mountainTask: List 4 primary causes of environmental degradation and state why environmental conservation is a collective social responsibility.
skyTitle: Jadav Payeng 'Forest Man of India' Case Study
skyTask: Analyze the personal environmental contribution of Jadav Payeng in creating a 1,360-acre man-made forest, illustrating individual impact.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Believing that environmental protection is solely the responsibility of government agencies rather than individual citizens.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'How did a single individual, Jadav Payeng, plant an entire forest?' Highlight individual environmental stewardship.

crossCurricularLinks: Environmental Law & Anthropology: Indigenous Conservation (Studying legal bio-reserve protections and traditional Sacred Groves)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Analyzes ecosystem factors, biodiversity conservation, sacred groves, and environmental protection laws.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 10: Organize local biodiversity documentation drives in school neighborhoods.

subject: science2
loDesc: Evaluates thermal, nuclear, hydroelectric, wind, and solar power generation mechanisms, comparing environmental impacts of fossil fuels versus eco-friendly renewable energy.
hookDemo: Display schematic flowcharts of a Thermal Power Plant vs a Solar Photovoltaic Power Plant.
hookAsk: Why does thermal power generation release harmful CO2 and SO2 pollutants, whereas solar photovoltaic generation produces clean zero-emission electricity?
streamDo: Observe energy generation types: Coal, Uranium, Water reservoir, Wind turbine, Solar PV panel, Natural Gas.
streamTask: Classify power plants into Fossil Fuel Based vs Green Renewable Energy categories.
mountainTask: Explain Uranium-235 nuclear fission chain reaction, detailing reactor core components, moderators, and radioactive waste disposal risks.
skyTitle: Hydroelectric Plant Efficiency & Ecological Impact Analysis
skyTask: Explain energy transformations in a Hydroelectric plant (Potential -> Kinetic -> Mechanical -> Electrical) and debate ecological pros vs cons of large dam reservoirs.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Assuming hydroelectric power generation is 100% eco-friendly without any environmental or social drawbacks.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'What happens to submerged forests and displaced communities when large dams are built?' Discuss reservoir ecological impacts.

crossCurricularLinks: Power Engineering & Environmental Economics: Energy Grid Transition (Comparing fossil fuel thermal emissions with solar/wind grid integration)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Evaluates power generation technologies, energy conversions, and environmental impacts of energy sources.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use small solar cell panels and toy motor fans for hands-on photovoltaic generation tests.

subject: science2
loDesc: Classifies kingdom Animalia based on body symmetry, germ layers, coelom, and body segmentation across 10 non-chordate phyla (Porifera to Hemichordata) and Chordata subphyla/classes.
hookDemo: Display preserved laboratory specimens: Sponge (Porifera), Jellyfish (Cnidaria), Tapeworm (Platyhelminthes), Earthworm (Annelida), Starfish (Echinodermata).
hookAsk: How do body symmetry (Radial vs Bilateral) and presence of a true body cavity (Eucoelomate) differentiate these phyla?
streamDo: Observe unique characteristics: Ostia/Osculum, Cnidocytes, Jointed appendages, Water vascular system, Notochord.
streamTask: Match unique features with their corresponding animal phylum (Porifera, Cnidaria, Arthropoda, Echinodermata, Chordata).
mountainTask: Construct a 4-point comparison table contrasting Non-Chordates and Chordates based on Notochord, Nerve Cord, Pharyngeal Gill Slits, and Heart position.
skyTask: Differentiate Vertebrate classes (Cyclostomata, Pisces, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia) using respiration organ, skin covering, and heart chamber criteria.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing Notochord (dorsal supporting rod in chordates) with Nerve Cord (central nervous system structure).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Which rod provides structural skeletal support, and which one transmits nerve impulses?'

crossCurricularLinks: Taxonomy & Evolutionary Biology: Comparative Anatomy (Systematizing animal phyla based on germ layers and body cavity evolution)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Classifies animal kingdom phyla based on germ layers, symmetry, coelom, and chordate features.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use preserved museum specimens for hands-on animal taxonomy identification.

subject: science2
loDesc: Investigates industrial microbiology applications: Applied Microbiology, Dairy Products (Cheese, Yogurt, Probiotics), Bread making, Vinegar production, Microbial Enzymes, and Bioremediation.
hookDemo: Display commercial probiotic drink bottles alongside a laboratory fermentation vessel diagram.
hookAsk: Why are live beneficial bacterial strains (Lactobacillus acidophilus) added to probiotic foods, and how do they improve gut health?
streamDo: Observe products/processes: Yogurt, Cheese, Vinegar (Acetic acid), Xanthan gum, Oil spill cleanup.
streamTask: Match products with their specific microbe strains (Lactobacillus bulgaricus, Acetobacter, Pseudomonas).
mountainTask: Explain the two-stage microbial production of Vinegar: Ethanol production by Yeast fermentation followed by Acetic Acid conversion by Acetobacter.
skyTask: Explain how Hydrocarbonoclastic Bacteria (HCB like Alcanivorax) clean ocean crude oil spills and how microbes treat sewage waste.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Believing all industrial food processing involving bacteria produces spoiled or unsafe products.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'What turns milk into yogurt or produces cheese?' Highlight controlled beneficial fermentation.

crossCurricularLinks: Industrial Biotechnology & Environmental Engineering: Pollution Cleanup (Using hydrocarbonoclastic bacteria to digest ocean oil spills)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Investigates applied microbiology in food production, industrial enzymes, and environmental bioremediation.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Conduct curd and yogurt preparation observations in school science labs.

subject: science2
loDesc: Understands Cytology, Stem Cells (Embryonic and Adult stem cells, Stem Cell Banking), Biotechnology applications in Agriculture (Bt Cotton, Golden Rice), Medicine (Insulin, Vaccines, Gene Therapy), and Organ Donation ethics.
hookDemo: Display a schematic diagram of a pluripotent Stem Cell differentiating into Muscle, Blood, Nerve, and Liver cells.
hookAsk: What makes stem cells uniquely valuable in regenerative medicine and organ transplant therapies?
streamDo: Observe innovations: Bt Cotton, Golden Rice (Vitamin A rich), Humulin (Recombinant Insulin), Edible Vaccines, Interferon.
streamTask: Classify innovations into Agricultural Biotechnology vs Medical Biotechnology applications.
mountainTask: Differentiate Embryonic Stem Cells from Adult Stem Cells (bone marrow, umbilical cord blood) and explain stem cell banking preservation.
skyTask: Analyze bio-engineering principles of Bt Cotton (Bacillus thuringiensis toxin gene) and evaluate environmental risks vs yield benefits of GM crops.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing embryonic stem cells (pluripotent - can form any tissue) with adult stem cells (multipotent - limited tissue types).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Which stem cell type can differentiate into ALL 220+ human body cell types?' Highlight embryonic pluripotency.

crossCurricularLinks: Bioethics & Agricultural Engineering: Recombinant Technology (Evaluating genetic engineering in Bt Cotton and organ transplantation ethics)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Understands cytology, stem cell potency, recombinant DNA biotechnology, and ethical organ donation.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Organize student seminars on stem cell banking and organ donation awareness.

subject: science2
loDesc: Analyzes factors affecting social health, digital addiction risks (excessive smartphone use, cyberbullying, online gaming), stress management techniques, and government support initiatives.
hookDemo: Display a infographic chart showing physical, mental, and social health dimensions.
hookAsk: How does excessive continuous smartphone screen usage cause physical eye strain, sleep disruption, and social isolation?
streamDo: Observe habits: Physical exercise, Excessive selfie taking, Cyberbullying, Hobbies/Music, Liquor consumption.
streamTask: Classify habits into Positive Social Health Factors vs Harmful Addictive Behaviors.
mountainTask: List 4 physical and psychological risks associated with gaming addiction and explain cyber crime prevention measures.
skyTask: Formulate a practical student stress management routine combining Laughter clubs, Outdoor sports, Expressive arts, and Counseling support.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Viewing health as purely physical fitness, ignoring mental health and social relationships.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Can a physically fit person be unhealthy if they suffer from severe social isolation or digital addiction?'

crossCurricularLinks: Psychology & Cyber Security: Digital Wellness (Developing healthy screen-time limits and recognizing online cyber threats)

metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 10: Conduct interactive workshops on digital detox and cyber safety.

subject: science2
loDesc: Classifies disasters, analyzes disaster management cycle (Pre-disaster phase vs Post-disaster phase), first-aid protocols (CPR, bandaging, transport of victims), and emergency response organization.
hookDemo: Display a diagram of the Disaster Management Cycle: Preparation -> Redemption -> Preparedness -> Response -> Resurgence -> Rehabilitation.
hookAsk: Why is Pre-disaster management planning (preparedness and mock drills) more effective in saving lives than Post-disaster relief work alone?
streamDo: Observe events: Tsunami, Cyclones, Forest Fires, Nuclear Accidents, Pandemics, Terrorism.
streamTask: Classify disaster events into Geological, Biological, Climate-related, or Man-made categories.
mountainTask: Describe 4 emergency patient transport methods (Cradle method, Human crutch, Stretcher, Chair method) and list essential kit supplies.
skyTask: Design a step-by-step school mock drill procedure for earthquake emergency evacuation, detailing warning signals, assembly points, and rescue squad roles.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Focusing disaster management efforts entirely on post-disaster rescue and relief while neglecting pre-disaster planning.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Which phase prevents casualties BEFORE a disaster strikes?' Emphasize pre-disaster preparedness and mock drills.

crossCurricularLinks: Public Safety & Civic Administration: Emergency Preparedness (Executing school evacuation drills and first-aid victim transport)
